pathogen: Cercospora zeae-maydis Tehon & E.Y. Daniels and/or Cercospora zeina Crous & U. Braun

egypt_evidence_status.interpretation: The Egypt-only search did not locate a reliable Egyptian maize field survey, isolate record, or official distribution entry specifically confirming GLS caused by C. zeae-maydis or C. zeina. Do not confuse Egyptian records of Cercospora beticola on sugar beet or Cephalosporium maydis, the late-wilt pathogen of maize, with maize GLS.
egypt_evidence_status.regional_context: GLS is well documented in maize-growing regions of Africa, but the reviewed continental sources did not establish Egypt as a confirmed GLS location.
egypt_evidence_status.diagnostic_priority: Any suspected Egyptian case should be confirmed by microscopy, isolation, and/or PCR before being labelled GLS.

early_stage: Tiny pinpoint brown, tan, or dark moist-looking spots
Small lesions may have a thin yellow chlorotic halo
Early lesions can be translucent when the leaf is held against light
mature_stage: Grey, tan, or brown lesions running parallel to the leaf veins
Lesion width is limited by adjacent secondary and tertiary veins
Mature lesions become opaque and may show small dark fungal sporulation points
advanced_stage: Lesions merge into large grey-brown blotches
Large areas of leaf tissue become necrotic
Whole leaves may blight, dry, and die prematurely
Severe upper-canopy infection can weaken stalks and increase lodging risk
image_annotation_targets: dark sporulation points on lesion surfaces

lesion_dimensions.reported_general_range: Approximately 5–70 mm long and 2–4 mm wide, with substantial variation among host genotypes and pathogen populations.
lesion_dimensions.egypt_specific_measurement: Not available from the Egypt-only sources reviewed.

distribution_on_plant: Typically begins on lower leaves before or around flowering and progresses upward during continued warm, humid weather. Egypt-specific canopy distribution has not been confirmed by a located field survey.
affected_parts: stalk indirectly through weakening and lodging
progression: Pinpoint lesions appear on lower leaves, sometimes surrounded by a yellow halo.
Lesions enlarge into narrow rectangular bands parallel to the leaf veins.
The lesions become grey, tan, or brown and may develop dark sporulation points.
Lesions merge and destroy increasing areas of leaf tissue.
Severe infection before grain filling can cause premature leaf death, reduced photosynthesis, stalk weakening, and poor grain development.

environment.humidity: High humidity, frequent dew, fog, and extended periods of leaf wetness favour infection and lesion development.
environment.temperature: Warm conditions around 25–30 °C are generally favourable; an Egypt-specific optimum was not identified.
environment.leaf_wetness: Prolonged wet leaves support spore germination and repeated infection cycles.
environment.residue: The pathogen can survive and produce inoculum on infected maize residue at the soil surface.
environment.egypt_context: These conditions may occur in irrigated or humid Egyptian maize environments, but this is a biological-risk interpretation, not evidence of confirmed Egyptian GLS prevalence.

similar_diseases.name: Northern Leaf Blight
similar_diseases.visual_difference: Long grey-green to tan cigar-shaped lesions, generally broader and less sharply rectangular than GLS lesions.

similar_diseases.name: Maydis Leaf Blight / Southern Leaf Blight
similar_diseases.visual_difference: Usually produces smaller tan or brown diamond-shaped lesions that may become rectangular, but typically lacks the sharply grey, vein-limited GLS appearance.

similar_diseases.name: Late Wilt of Maize
similar_diseases.visual_difference: Causes systemic yellowing, wilting, vascular browning, and plant death rather than characteristic rectangular leaf lesions. It is documented in Egypt but is not GLS.

similar_diseases.name: Cercospora Leaf Spot of Sugar Beet
similar_diseases.visual_difference: Can produce Cercospora-type spots on sugar beet in Egypt but is a different host-pathogen disease and should not be used as evidence for maize GLS.

recommended_image_search_terms: suspected gray leaf spot maize Egypt
maize gray leaf spot rectangular vein limited lesions
maize GLS grey tan lesions leaf veins
diagnostic_caution: This JSON records a limited or unconfirmed Egypt-specific status. Rectangular grey lesions alone are not sufficient to establish GLS in Egypt because other foliar diseases can resemble it. Laboratory confirmation and a documented Egyptian host/pathogen record are recommended.

research_notes: This is intentionally a conservative Egypt-only record. It avoids treating global GLS symptom descriptions or Egyptian Cercospora diseases on other crops as proof that maize GLS is established in Egypt.
